definitions.explanation: A record of events, activities, or observations kept on a daily basis, typically in a professional, institutional, or organizational context. Unlike a personal diary, a {日誌|にっし} is usually an official or work-related record.

examples.japanese: {業務|ぎょうむ}{日誌|にっし}を{書|か}く。
{毎日|まいにち}{日誌|にっし}をつけるのが{日課|にっか}だ。
examples.english: Keeping a daily log is part of my routine.

examples.japanese: {工事|こうじ}{現場|げんば}では{作業|さぎょう}{日誌|にっし}の{記入|きにゅう}が{義務|ぎむ}づけられている。
examples.english: At construction sites, filling out a daily work log is mandatory.

examples.japanese: {航海|こうかい}{日誌|にっし}には{天候|てんこう}や{海|うみ}の{状態|じょうたい}が{細|こま}かく{記録|きろく}されていた。
examples.english: The ship's log had detailed records of the weather and sea conditions.

notes:
Composed of {日|にっ} (day) and {誌|し} (record, chronicle). The word emphasizes systematic, daily record-keeping in a professional or institutional setting. It is distinct from {日記|にっき} (personal diary), which is more private and reflective.

Various types of {日誌|にっし} are standard practice in Japanese workplaces and institutions: {業務|ぎょうむ}{日誌|にっし} (work log), {保育|ほいく}{日誌|にっし} (childcare log at nurseries), {航海|こうかい}{日誌|にっし} (ship's log), and {学級|がっきゅう}{日誌|にっし} (class diary, kept by students on rotation).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {業務|ぎょうむ}{日誌|にっし}: work log, operations log
- {航海|こうかい}{日誌|にっし}: ship's log
- {作業|さぎょう}{日誌|にっし}: work/operations diary
- {学級|がっきゅう}{日誌|にっし}: class diary
- {日誌|にっし}をつける: to keep a daily log
- {日誌|にっし}に{記入|きにゅう}する: to fill in the daily log

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {日記|にっき}: diary — a personal diary; more subjective and private than {日誌|にっし}
- {記録|きろく}: record — broader term for any kind of record, not necessarily daily
- {報告書|ほうこくしょ}: report — a formal written report, typically about a specific topic rather than daily routine
